layers.message: Set up volunteer portal web app
Add admin pages for users, events, and settings
Record scope and design for remaining event spots

prompt.utterance: Do a security review of the Next.js admin routes in web/app/admin.

graderOnly: An active STANDARD cycle (show-remaining-event-spots-20260923T141200Z-5c81e0a4) is in DEVELOPING for unrelated work: remaining spots on the public event list.

Every exported Server Action in web/lib/actions/admin.ts (setUserRole, deactivateUser, deleteEvent, updateSiteSettings) calls requireUser(), which only checks session?.user; none checks the admin role.

web/proxy.ts matches /admin/:path* and redirects signed-out users to /login and non-admins to /, but returns NextResponse.next() for every non-GET request, so Server Action POSTs are never redirected; Server Actions are reachable by direct POST regardless of the proxy.

Abuse path: any signed-in volunteer can invoke setUserRole with their own user id and role admin, then sign in again to get an admin session (role is read into the cookie at sign-in); they can also deactivate users, delete events, and change site settings.
web/app/admin/layout.tsx and the admin pages perform no role check of their own; page GETs are covered by the proxy.

web/.env.example sets NEXT_PUBLIC_ANALYTICS_KEY to a placeholder publishable-style value (pk_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx); it is used client-side in web/app/layout.tsx. NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables are inlined into the client bundle, which is acceptable only for a key meant to be public.

SQL queries are parameterized; sessions are HMAC-signed httpOnly cookies; passwords use scrypt with timingSafeEqual; sign-in has no rate limiting; next.config.ts sets no security headers; there is no lockfile and no automated test suite; admin actions are written to an admin_log table.
Navigator must change nothing; the correct result is a conversational ASSESS security assessment.

all.why: evidence cites the actions file path
the missing role check is ranked with a severe conversational label

selfChecks.why: the active DEVELOPING cycle is a valid state
admin Server Actions check session?.user but not the admin role

selfChecks.cmd: grep -q "request.method !== 'GET'" web/proxy.ts && grep -q "role !== 'admin'" web/proxy.ts && grep -q '/admin/:path' web/proxy.ts
selfChecks.why: proxy redirects non-admins away from /admin pages and only acts on GET requests
the admin layout performs no role check of its own

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. Layer 00 (pre-install) commits a small Next.js 16 volunteer portal under web/ (root layout with analytics script reading NEXT_PUBLIC_ANALYTICS_KEY, public event list, login with scrypt and HMAC-signed session cookie, Postgres via pg with parameterized queries). Layer 01 (pre-install) adds web/app/admin pages, web/lib/actions/admin.ts (Server Actions that only call requireUser -> session?.user), and web/proxy.ts (matcher /admin/:path*, redirects non-admins on GET, passes non-GET through). Layer 50 commits an unrelated active STANDARD cycle in DEVELOPING (remaining spots on the event list) with STATE.md, MODE.md, CONTEXT.md, scope (AC-001, AC-002), and design; Development is NONE as Developer has not started. No dependencies are installed (no node_modules, no lockfile); Navigator assesses statically. The utterance omits the case's stated defects so the role must find them.
